title: Massage & Yoga for Tinies
strapline: Gentle stretches and story-massage for our youngest — nurturing touch and slow movement that soothe, connect and settle.
intent: Babies and toddlers experience warm, respectful, consented touch that soothes, regulates and builds secure attachment.
Children learn slow, playful yoga-style movements that stretch, ground and calm a busy little body.
Children develop body awareness — where their arms, legs and tummy are — through gentle massage and movement.
Children wind down before sleep or after high-energy play, easing the transition to rest.
Children build a trusting bond with their key person through unhurried, attuned one-to-one time.
implementation: Always ask and read the cues — 'shall we do our massage?' — and stop the moment a child signals no; consent is taught here from the start.
Keep it playful and story-led: 'round and round the garden' on the palm, 'the wheels on the bus' with gentle strokes down the arms.
Use simple animal yoga for toddlers — be a cat stretching, a butterfly, a sleepy bear — modelled slowly with a warm voice.
Do it skin-safe over clothes for older babies; follow your setting's touch, hygiene and safeguarding policy at all times.
Time it well — after nappy changes, before sleep, or to settle after a busy morning — as part of a calm, predictable rhythm.
Slow your own voice and breathing right down; the adult's calm is the most powerful ingredient.
key_questions: Shall we do our stretches — arms up high like a tree?
Can you feel the gentle strokes down your arm?
Would you like the massage today, or not right now?
Can you be a sleepy bear curling up small?
Does your body feel soft and calm now?

impact.text: Children build warm bonds with their key person and are comforted by familiar adults.
Children express emotions and are soothed through responsive co-regulation and touch.
Children gain control of their body — reaching, stretching, moving with growing awareness.
Children settle into predictable rhythms of rest and calm with responsive care.
Children respond to gentle songs and rhymes with delight, anticipating familiar refrains.

enhancements: A story-massage routine tied to a favourite rhyme, done the same way each day so it becomes a soothing ritual.
Soft, slow background music and dimmed lighting to signal wind-down time.
Animal yoga picture cards for toddlers to choose the next pose.
A shared routine sent home so parents can do the same calming massage at bedtime.
A cosy floor space with mats and cushions kept clear for stretching and rolling.

playing_exploring: Babies explore touch, movement and their own bodies through gentle, playful interaction.
Toddlers enjoy copying animal poses, exploring what their bodies can do slowly.
active_learning: The soothing, connected experience motivates children to seek this calm time again.
Children settle and self-regulate more readily as the ritual becomes familiar.
creating_thinking: Children begin to link the massage and stretches with feeling calm and ready to rest.
Toddlers anticipate the next move in a familiar routine, holding the sequence in mind.
